messages:
Avery J.: Heads up 12; IndieDev LLC submitted invoice IDV-2026-77 for $7,500 but refuses to provide a W-9/TIN citing privacy concerns. They say they 'prefer direct deposit only' and gave no TIN. Should we pay in full or start backup withholding?

Priya T.: If they're a US person/entity doing work in the US, IRS rules require a W-9. If we don't have a TIN, we may be required to apply backup withholding at 24% on reportable payments. Need to confirm the payee type: US LLC taxed as disregarded vs corp matters.

Avery J.: Vendor record lists them as "IndieDev LLC" with a US address and bank in US. No TIN on file. Contact says they will not send a signed W-9 PDF.

CJ M.: We can't accept refusal. Our vendor onboarding requires a completed W-9 for US payees. If they refuse, legally we must either (A) refuse payment; or (B) apply backup withholding and report to IRS on 1099/1099-NEC as appropriate. Also consider whether they're a corporation (exempt from 1099 reporting).

Priya T.: Quick checks: 1) Ask vendor if they are a corporation (C-Corp/S-Corp) or disregarded entity; if corp, 1099 not required. 2) If not corp and no TIN, backup withholding applies. 3) Document outreach attempts.

Avery J.: I tried to call and they said they won't provide SSN/EIN on email. They suggested sharing a masked TIN (last 4 digits) only. That won't satisfy our compliance.

Tax-bot: Tax note: Per IRS Pub 1281 and backup withholding rules, payers must withhold 24% on reportable payments to payees who fail to furnish a TIN. Exceptions exist (e.g., corporations). Backup withholding should be deposited and reported; keep records of W-9 requests.

CJ M.: Recommended next step: send a formal request for W-9 with a 7-business-day deadline. If no W-9, either (1) initiate backup withholding 24% and pay the net amount, or (2) hold payment until documentation provided. Also copy Legal to escalation if vendor threatens to stop work.

Avery J.: Draft message below. Priya/CJ please review: 

"Hi IndieDev team 12; thanks for invoice IDV-2026-77. Redwood requires a completed IRS Form W-9 (with legal name and TIN) for US payees to process payments. We cannot accept masked TINs. Please return a signed W-9 within 7 business days. If we do not receive a valid W-9, Redwood will either (a) place the invoice on hold until documentation is provided, or (b) process payment subject to backup withholding at the IRS rate (currently 24%), and report the payment to the IRS as required. If you believe you are exempt from 1099/reporting (e.g., a corporation), please state your tax classification and provide supporting documentation (e.g., articles of incorporation).

Regards, Avery on behalf of Redwood AP"

Priya T.: Looks good. Add a line asking for the vendor's tax classification checkbox (Individual/Sole Proprietor/Partnership/C-Corp/S-Corp/LLC taxed as corp) so we can triage.

Avery J.: Updated and sent at 2026-01-11T09:18:04Z to payments@indiedev.example.

AP-bot: Outbound message posted to payments@indiedev.example; invoice IDV-2026-77 flagged for W-9 request. AP hold not yet applied.

Avery J.: Vendor responded: "We will not send W-9. Send payment or we stop work." No other details.

CJ M.: Do not capitulate. If they stop work, that's a commercial issue but not a legal reason to ignore IRS requirements. Proceed with backup withholding if they refuse to provide W-9. Also notify Procurement to pause future engagements with them until resolved.

Priya T.: I'll prepare the ledger treatment for backup withholding: withhold 24% of $7,500 = $1,800. We can either pay $5,700 net now and remit $1,800 to IRS, or hold full amount and remit when/if required. Recommend pay net minus withholding to avoid breach of services if we want continuity.

Avery J.: What's the reporting cadence? If we withhold, we still file 1099-NEC with the vendor's TIN missing — does that create issues?

Tax-bot: If the TIN is missing, you attach Form 945/ backup withholding deposits and file Form 1099-B/1099-NEC with the vendor's details as available. The vendor can later provide TIN and reconcile. Keep written proof of W-9 requests and vendor refusal; IRS may accept documentation if vendor later claims incorrectly withheld.

CJ M.: I'm ok authorizing backup withholding if Procurement and contracts are informed. We'll need a short escalation note to Procurement and Legal to consider termination if vendor non-compliance persists.

Avery J.: OK applying backup withholding and issuing net payment today. AP-bot, please set hold flag to indicate backup withholding applied and record withheld amount. Also cc procurement.

AP-bot: Action: backup withholding applied to IDV-2026-77. Gross $7,500, withheld $1,800 (24%), net payable $5,700. AP queue notified. Procurement notified.

Avery J.: Logging internal note in vendor record. Closing thread 12; reopen if vendor provides W-9 or disputes withholding. :white_check_mark:
